title: 2004 AMC 12A Problem 9

concepts.label: Power scaling of length, area, and volume

statement: A company sells peanut butter in cylindrical jars. Marketing research suggests that using wider jars will increase sales. If the diameter of the jars is increased by \(25\%\) without altering the volume, by what percent must the height be decreased?

solutions.text:
Multiplying the diameter by \(\tfrac54\) multiplies the base area by \(\left(\tfrac54\right)^2 = \tfrac{25}{16}.\)

To keep the volume fixed, the height must be multiplied by \(\tfrac{16}{25} = 0.64.\) That is a decrease of \(1 - 0.64 = 0.36,\) or \(36\%.\)

Thus, the correct answer is C.
hints: The base area scales with the square of the diameter
Multiplying the diameter by \(\tfrac54\) multiplies the base area by \(\left(\tfrac54\right)^2\)
